articleTitle: A 350 GHz SIS Receiver on the Nobeyama 10 m Submillimeter Telescope
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have developed a low-noise submillimeter-wave SIS receiver (320–360 GHz) for a 10 m submillimeter telescope, which was installed at Nobeyama in 2000 February. This receiver and a millimeter-wave SIS receiver are mounted on the ceiling of the Cassegrain receiver cabin of the 10 m telescope. Two curved mirrors couple a shaped Cassegrain beam from the subreflector to mixer horns. The minimum noise temperature measured in front of the receiver was 52 K in double sideband (DSB) at a local oscillator (LO) frequency of 354 GHz, which corresponds to three-times quantum limits (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3h\nu/k_{\rm{B}}$</tex>). This noise temperature contributions are resolved into the optics, mixer, and IF parts. The temperature ripple of a two-stage Gifford–McMahon cryocooler has been reduced to be 2 mK peak-to-peak at the mixer block with a helium pot temperature stabilizer. Mechanical vibration (30 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> peak-to-peak) of the cold head degrades the receiver stability.

articleTitle: Convection-Dominated, Magnetized Accretion Flows into Black Holes
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) hydrodynamical simulations have been intensively performed recently to clarify the accretion-flow structure in the low-radiation-efficiency limit. However, the results depend critically on the parameterized magnitude of the viscosity, which, in principle, should be determined self-consistently by MHD simulations. We analyzed the structure of 3D MHD accretion flows initially threaded by weak toroidal magnetic fields, and found for the first time large-scale convective motions dominating near to the black hole. Radial profiles of each physical quantity include: the density, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \rho \propto r^{-0.5}$</tex>; radial velocity, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ v_r\propto r^{-1.5}$</tex>; temperature, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ T \propto r^{-1.0}$</tex>; and field strength, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ B^2 \propto r^{-1.5}$</tex>. Although the flow structure, itself, appears to be similar to those obtained by hydrodynamic simulations, the observational appearance is distinct. Unlike non-magnetic models, in which radiation is dominant at the outermost convective zones because of outward energy flow by convection, substantial accretion energy can be released in the vicinity of a black hole in MHD flow via magnetic reconnection. Such reconnection leads to sporadic flare events, thus producing variability in out-going radiation, as is commonly observed in objects with black-hole accretion.

articleTitle: Viscous Transonic Decretion in Disks of Be Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We consider the characteristics of the outflow in disks of Be stars, based on the viscous decretion disk scenario. In this scenario, the matter ejected from the equatorial surface of a star drifts outward because of the effect of viscosity, and forms the disk. For simplicity, we adopt the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \alpha$</tex>-prescription for the viscous stress, and assume the disk to be isothermal. Solving the resulting wind equations, we find that a transonic solution exists for any value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \alpha$</tex>. The sonic point is located at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r > 100\;R$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ r > 100\;R$</tex> for the plausible values of parameters, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ R$</tex> is the stellar radius. The sonic radius is smaller for a higher temperature and/or a larger radiative force. We also find that the topology of the sonic point is nodal for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \alpha >rsim 0.95$</tex>, while it is of the saddle type for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \alpha \lesssim 0.9$</tex>. We expect that the sonic point in the former case is unstable, whereas that in the latter case is stable. The outflow is highly subsonic in the inner part of the disk. Roughly, the outflow velocity increases linearly with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ r$</tex> and the surface density decreases as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ r^{-2}$</tex>. Interestingly, the disk is near-Keplerian in the inner subsonic region, while it is angular-momentum conserving in the outer subsonic region and in the supersonic region. Our results, together with the observed range of the base density for Be star disks, suggest that the mass-loss rate in the equatorial region is at most comparable with that in the polar region.

articleTitle: Amplification of Magnetic Fields in an Accretion Disk with a Starburst Torus
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: It is widely believed that a black hole is surrounded by an accretion disk. Such an accretion disk should have magnetic fields whose evolution is important to understand the disk dynamics, since the viscosity in the disk must originate from magnetic turbulence. In the case of the accretion disk of AGN (active galactic nuclei) with a circum-disk star-burst region, we point out that the so-called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \alpha $</tex>-dynamo effect via radiation drag due to an exterior radiation field around the disk works well. This is possible since the drag time-scale is longer than the dynamical time-scale. Importantly, we find that the starburst AGN satisfies this criterion. Thus, the magnetic field of the accretion disk of the starburst AGN is amplified by the dynamo effect owing to the radiation drag. This results in enhancing the mass-accretion rate to the massive black-hole of AGN within the star-burst region.

articleTitle: A Graph-Theoretical Approach for Quantifying Two-Dimensional Galaxy Distributions and Comparison with Cold Dark Matter Universe
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: With the help of a graph-theoretical approach, we have quantified two-dimensional galaxy distributions in observation and Cold Dark Matter (CDM) simulations. In our analysis, we adopted the Lyon–Meudon Extragalactic Database as a typical two-dimensional observation. To estimate adjacency matrices, we constructed constellation graphs from galaxy distributions, and calculated the distribution functions of the eigenvalues of these matrices. Using the mean absolute deviations, we compared the two-dimensional galaxy distributions in observations with CDM simulations in a statistical way. From our analysis we found that the CDM model with a density parameter of less than one is preferable to reproduce the galaxy distributions in the observations.

articleTitle: CO Column Density and Extinction in the Chamaeleon II–III Dark-Cloud Complex
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 - 0$</tex>) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{C}{{18\atop} \rm{O}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 - 0$</tex>) observations of the Chamaeleon II-III dark-cloud complex with the NANTEN radio telescope. The column densities of both molecular isotopes were derived assuming LTE. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V}$</tex> values were obtained by scaling the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{J}$</tex> values that were derived using an adaptive-grid star-count method applied to the DENIS <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-band data. We established the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V}-$</tex>CO isotope column-density relations in Cha II and III, and compared them with those in Cha I. The slopes of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V}$</tex>-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CO relations for Cha II and III are steeper than that for Cha I. Those of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V} - \rm{C}{{18\atop} \rm{O}}$</tex> relations are similar among the three clouds. The total column density ratio, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N({{13\atop} \rm{CO}})/N(\rm{C}{{18\atop} \rm{O}})$</tex>, in Cha I tends to be small compared with those in Cha II or Cha III; the ratios range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 5$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 25$</tex> at low extinction in Cha II and III, but at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10$</tex> in Cha I. We suggest that the increase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N({{13\atop} \rm{C}}{{\atop} \rm{O}})$</tex> due to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} \rm{C}}{{\atop} \rm{O}}$</tex> formation process causes cloud-to-cloud variations in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V} - N({{13\atop} \rm{C}}{{\atop} \rm{O}})$</tex> correlation.

articleTitle: Tidal Truncation of Gas Replenishment and Global Suppression of Galactic Star Formation in Distant Clusters
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Recent spectroscopic observations of galaxies in distant clusters have revealed that the rate of star formation in star-forming galaxies is significantly suppressed with respect to their counterparts in the field at a similar redshift. It is, however, highly uncertain which physical processes are responsible for this suppression. We present the results of a numerical investigation of how the global tidal field of a cluster dynamically influences the reservoir of halo gas surrounding a disk galaxy as it falls into the cluster from the surrounding field. We find that the tidal field of the cluster efficiently removes the halo gas from the galaxy, thereby halting its accretion onto the disk, and thus the fueling of star formation within. This effectively truncates the galaxy’s star formation. We also find that this tidal truncation does not depend very strongly on the orbit of the disk with respect to the center of the cluster. These results suggest that the global tidal field of clusters is capable of causing a widespread and uniform suppression of star formation in galaxies accreted by the cluster. In light of these results, we discuss the importance of this tidal truncation of the gas supply in the formation of S0 galaxies in clusters.

articleTitle: Twin Jets as a Potential Distance Detector
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A preview study of using observational data of the proper motions and Doppler-shifted velocities of twin jets to determine the distance of sources inside and outside our Galaxy is made. We investigate the feasibility of this method by studying the uncertainty of the distance caused by the uncertainties of the measured quantities. It shows that, when the motion of components of the jet is relativistic, the uncertainty of the distance is within the same order of the uncertainties of the measured values of the proper motions and Doppler-shifted velocities. In particular, when assuming that the pattern speed equals the flow speed in the jet, for 10% uncertainties of the measured quantities, the uncertainty of the distance caused by them would be well within 13%. With the current technique, this method is realizable. For the convenience of choosing the sources to observe, some sources as potential targets are also listed in this paper.

articleTitle: ASCA Observation of the Nearest Gravitational Lensing Cluster Candidate — A 3408
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed the nearest gravitational lensing cluster candidate, A 3408 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0.042$</tex>), with ASCA. The projected mass profile of A 3408 was determined from the ICM temperature and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-model parameters obtained with ASCA, assuming that the hot gas is spherically symmetric and in hydrostatic equilibrium. The projected mass within an arc radius, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{\rm arc}$</tex>, of 110 kpc is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M(r_{\rm arc}) = 1.2^{+0.8}_{-0.4} \times 10^{13} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$ </tex>. This is 18–45% of the mass previously derived from a lensing analysis by Campusano et al. (, AAA 069.160.189) without any X-ray information.The primary cause of this discrepancy is in their assumption that the center of the cluster potential coincides with the position of the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), while we reveal the BCG position to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60^{\prime\prime}$</tex> outside of the X-ray center. We further calculated a model for the source galaxy position and the gravitational potential that can reproduce both the X-ray data and the arc image. In this model, the magnification factor of the lens for the source galaxy was evaluated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta m = 0.07 \pm 0.03 \,\rm{mag}$</tex>; i.e., the source galaxy is slightly magnified by the lens cluster A 3408.

articleTitle: Spectral Variations of Cyg X-1 in the Hard State Studied with ASCA Data
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Spectral variations of Cyg X-1 in the hard state have been studied on two time scales of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{4} \, {\rm s}$</tex> and 1 s using ASCA archive data. The energy spectrum was well fit by a model consisting of a multicolor blackbody expected from an optically-thick accretion disk and a broken power-law, with absorption by interstellar matter. The broken power-law component was found to change its normalization on both time scales, while keeping the spectral shape unchanged, whereas the multicolor blackbody component varies only on a time scale of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^4 \, {\rm s}$</tex>. From this clear separation of the time variabilities, the two spectral components can be considered to be two real substances reflecting two respective emission processes different from each other. We found from a careful comparison of the disk parameters that the innermost radius in the hard state is a few times larger than that in the soft state, even if the uncertainty in a ratio of the observed color temperature to an effective temperature is taken into account. It is suggested that an optically-thin disk exists inside the optically-thick disk in the hard state and that the broken power-law component comes from the optically-thin inner disk.

articleTitle: Polarization and Variations of BL Lacertae Objects
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: BL Lacertae objects are an extreme subclass of AGNs showing rapid and large-amplitude variability, high and variable polarization, and core-dominated radio emissions. If a strong beaming effect is the cause of the extreme observation properties, one would expect that these properties would be correlated with each other. Based on the relativistic beaming model, relationships between the polarization and the magnitude variation in brightness, as well as the core-dominance parameter are derived and used statistically to compare with the observational data of a BL Lacertae object sample. The statistical results are consistent with these correlations, which suggests that the polarization, the variation, and the core-dominance parameter are possible indications of the beaming effect.

articleTitle: Large-Amplitude 2.65-d Oscillation in the VY Scl-Type Star V425 Cassiopeiae
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: From long-term photometry of a VY Scl-type star, V425 Cas, between 1998 and 2000, we discovered a short-term, large-amplitude (up to 1.5 mag) variation. The variation was well represented by a single period of 2.65 d. The large amplitude and the profile of the folded light curve suggest that the dwarf nova-type disk instability is responsible for this variation. The shortness of the period is unprecedented in hydrogen-rich cataclysmic variables. Given the recent emerging evidence that the irradiation from white dwarfs in VY Scl-type systems affect their light behavior, we propose a possibility that this unique variation in V425 Cas can be explained by the combination of the dwarf nova-type disk instability and irradiation. Similar short-period “outbursts" have been known in X-ray transients (V518 Per), and helium cataclysmic variables (CR Boo and V803 Cen). We discuss the possibility that these phenomena have a common origin to the unique variation in V425 Cas.

articleTitle: The FR-I Radio Galaxies NGC 315 and NGC 4261 Observed with ASCA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: FR-I radio galaxies NGC 315 and NGC 4261 were observed in X-rays with ASCA for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 37 ~\rm{ks}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 54~\rm{ks}$</tex>, respectively. Hard X-ray emission from a point-like source at the nucleus was detected at a 2–10 keV luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.1 \times 10^{41}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.2 \times 10^{40}~\rm{erg}~\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, respectively, for assumed distances of 66 Mpc and 29 Mpc (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_0 = 75~\rm{km}~\rm{s}^{-1}~\rm{Mpc}^{-1}$</tex>). The 2–10 keV spectra of NGC 315 and NGC 4261 were both fitted successfully with a power-law of photon index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.02 \pm 0.34$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.45 \pm 0.11$</tex>, respectively, plus emission from hot gas. The NGC 315 nucleus is mildly absorbed. No X-ray variability was detected from either object, with typical upper limits of several tens per cent. These results imply the presence of a low-luminosity active galactic nucleus in both galaxies, and reconfirm the previous recognition that the FR-I nuclei are significantly less X-ray luminous than the FR-II ones.

articleTitle: The Ortho-to-Para Ratio and the Chemical Properties of C3 H2 in Dark Cloud Cores
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have observed cyclic C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_{K_{a}K_{c}}= 2_{12}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1_{01}, 2_{02}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1_{11}, 3_{12}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3_{03}$</tex>) lines at the 3 mm wavelength region toward the starless TMC-1C cloud and the protostellar core of L 1527 with the 45 m telescope at Nobeyama Radio Observatory. In both clouds, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2_{12}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1_{01}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2_{02}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1_{11}$</tex> lines are strongly detected, while the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3_{12}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3_{03}$</tex> line is only detected toward the center of the protostellar core L 1527. From our statistical equilibrium analyses of the ortho-C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2_{12}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1_{01}$</tex>) and the para-C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2_{02}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1_{11}$</tex>) lines, the ortho-to-para ratios of C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex> are determined to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.4\pm0.1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5\pm0.5$</tex> in TMC-1C and L 1527, respectively. These values are lower than the statistical value of 3, although the error of the ratio in L 1527 is large. Since thermal equilibrium with a dust temperature of 10 K still gives a ratio of 3 in c-C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex>, this result should suggest the lower ortho-to-para ratio of the precursor molecule, c-C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{3}^{+}$</tex>, which is thought to be mainly produced by C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+} +$</tex> H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex>. Thus, we conclude that the lower ortho-to-para ratio of c-C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex> is due to a lower ortho-to-para ratio of H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> than the statistical value.

articleTitle: Absorption Measurement of Hydrogen Molecules in the Early Universe
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigate the observability of hydrogen molecules in absorption. The absorption efficiency of hydrogen molecules becomes comparable with, or larger than, that of the dust grains in the metal-poor condition expected in the early Universe. If we can use bright infrared continuum sources behind the molecular-gas clouds, the absorption measurement of the hydrogen molecules could be an important technique to explore the primordial gas clouds that are contracting into first-generation objects.

articleTitle: A Molecular Cloud and an Expanding Cavity Adjacent to the Nonthermal Filaments of the Galactic Center Radio Arc
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Large-scale CO images taken with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 2$</tex> focal-plane array receiver on the 45 m telescope of Nobeyama Radio Observatory reveal parsec-scale structure of molecular gas around the Galactic center radio arc. The LVG analysis shows that the gas kinetic temperature is considerably enhanced (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm k} \geq 70 \,{\rm K}$</tex>) in CO 0.13–0.13, a cloud which seems to be in contact with the nonthermal filaments of the Galactic center radio arc. This lends support for an interaction between CO 0.13–0.13 and the nonthermal filaments. The interaction with the strong magnetic field in and around the nonthermal filaments may heat up the molecular gas in CO 0.13–0.13 through shock dissipation and/or magnetic viscosity.We also find an expanding cavity adjacent to the nonthermal filaments. The shell has a radius of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 5 \,\rm{pc}$</tex> and an expansion velocity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25 \,\rm{km} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. This expanding cavity might have been formed by several hundred supernovae or a single hypernova within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 \times 10^5 \,\rm{yr}$</tex>. Magnetic tubes in this region could have been swept up by the expanding cavity, and compressed by interactions with CO 0.13–0.13. An interaction between the cloud and magnetic field may accelerate electrons to relativistic energies through shock acceleration or magnetic field reconnection.

articleTitle: Water Maser Survey in the Andromeda Galaxy
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on a water maser survey in the Andromeda galaxy (M 31). The surveyed H II regions with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}$</tex>CO clouds are expected to be regions of ongoing star formation with water maser activity. Nevertheless, we could not detect any water maser emission with an upper limit of around 0.35 Jy or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.9\times 10^{-3}\,L_{{\odot}}$</tex> in isotropic luminosity. These results indicate a low activity of the present star formation in M 31.

articleTitle: Metallic Abundances in the Planet-Harboring G-Type Star HD 38529
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The abundances of 16 elements (C through Y) in the recently detected planet-harboring G4 IV star HD 38529 are presented. A spectroscopic analysis was carried out differentially relative to the Sun. The adopted atmospheric parameters of the star are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm eff} = 5500 \pm 100 ~ {\rm K}, \log g = 3.6 \pm 0.1, \xi_{\rm t}= 1.0 \pm 0.3 ~ {\rm km} ~ {\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>, and [M/H]<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$= +0.3$</tex>. Iron is definitely overabundant with respect to the Sun, [Fe/H]<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$= +0.40\pm0.06$</tex>, and all other elements are also found to be enhanced. The enhancements of iron peak elements (Ti through Ni) are coincident with that of Fe within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.1~$</tex>dex, while C and O are slightly less enhanced than Fe.

articleTitle: Temperature Map and Iron Abundance of the Ophiuchus Cluster of Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present an X-ray surface-brightness distribution and a temperature map of the Ophiuchus cluster of galaxies observed by ASCA. The Ophiuchus cluster is a nearby rich cluster located at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z= 0.028$</tex> having an angular extent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1 {{}^{\circ }}$</tex>. The observations were made by five pointings that cover the whole cluster. After deconvolution with the ASCA complex response function, we obtained the surface-brightness distribution with an angular resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${2{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex> and a temperature map with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${8{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex> resolution. The X-ray surface-brightness distribution shows a nearly spherically symmetric distribution, except for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15\sigma$</tex> image excess at the position of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${10{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex> to the north of the cluster center. On the other hand, a hot region with a temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 13 \,{\rm keV}$</tex> is spread over a region of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${20{}^{\rm {\prime }}}\times {30{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${20{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex> to the west of the cluster center. Because these characteristics are similar to those of the Coma cluster, we conclude this cluster has never relaxed dynamically, and is also recently experienced a merger.

articleTitle: A Large-Scale CO Mapping of the Central Region of W 51
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a high-resolution (16<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\prime\prime}$</tex>) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} \rm{CO}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J= 1$</tex>−<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>) map of the central region of W 51. We observed an area of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${15\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime }}3}\times {16\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime }}7}$</tex>, which covers the entire region of G49.5–0.4, the brightest source in the W 51 region. Four discrete molecular clouds were identified toward G49.5–0.4, and evidence of cloud–cloud collisions was found. We speculate that a “pileup” of three molecular clouds resulted in a burst of massive star formation in G49.5–0.4.

articleTitle: SiO Maser Survey in the Galactic Center Region with a Multi-Beam Receiver
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have made a wide-field survey of SiO masers in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7'' \times 13''$</tex> area around the Galactic center with the Nobeyama 45-m radio telescope using a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 3$</tex> multi-beam SIS mixer receiver at 43 GHz. We detected 9 SiO maser sources (6 of them are new); newly detected 6 sources have been identified with Miras or OH 1612 MHz maser sources. The source surface number density, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 360$</tex> per square degree, found in this survey is slightly smaller than the number density of OH 1612 MHz sources in the same area. A least-squares analysis of the radial velocities of the detected sources has revealed a rapid rotation of the stars around the Galactic center. This implies that most of the objects detected in this survey belong to the nuclear disk near the Galactic center.

articleTitle: Photometric Observation of a New in-the-Gap SU UMa-Type Dwarf Nova V 725 Aquilae during the 1999 Superoutburst
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report our photometric observation of the 1999 September outburst of a dwarf nova, V725 Aql. Our detection of superhumps established that it belongs to SUUMa stars. By performing a period analysis of the superhumps, we revealed a long superhump period of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.09909 \pm 0.00015\,\rm{d}$</tex>, which implies that its orbital period is well over 2 hr. The outburst light curve is typical for a superoutburst, though, after the superoutburst, the object experienced a re-brightening which can be seen in some SUUMa stars with short orbital periods. The 1999 superoutburst occurred about 1650 d after the last possible superoutburst in 1995. This indicates the supercycle of V725 Aql to be long, over 1000 d. This long supercycle implies a low mass-transfer rate of this star.

articleTitle: Contribution of Supernova Gamma-Rays to the Gamma-Ray Background Emission
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Diffuse <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma $</tex>-ray background emission has been observed by a number of satellites and balloons. The spectrum spreads over a wide range of photon energies, and the emission is almost isotropic. Although the origin of diffuse <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma $</tex>-ray background emission is still unclear, some candidates are suggested, such as Seyfert galaxies, blazars, and type-Ia supernovae. The type-Ia supernovae synthesize a large amount of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{56\atop}\rm{Ni}}$</tex>, which emit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma $</tex>-ray photons while decaying into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{56\atop}\rm{Co}}$</tex> and then to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{56\atop}\rm{Fe}}$</tex>, and thus emit strong <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma $</tex>-rays of energy around 1 MeV. We estimate the intensity of the diffuse <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma $</tex>-ray background emission from supernovae, and compare the result with the recent observation of COMPTEL. The resultant spectrum is too small to explain the observation, because it is only 10% of the observed flux, implying contributions from other sources.

articleTitle: Radiative Collimation of Electron–Positron Jets
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a novel mechanism for the collimation of relativistic outflows emanated from accretion disks via the disk radiation field, itself. In general, winds driven by disk radiation fields diverge, due to the effect of rotation and the nature of radiation. If, however, the disk is divided into an optically thin hot inner region and an optically thick luminous outer region, the outflow ejected from the inner disk is accelerated and collimated by radiation fields produced by the outer disk. Since this mechanism effectively works on electron–positron pair plasmas, in accretion disk systems with inner hot advection-dominated regions, electron–positron jets easily form on the disk-rotation axis. For pure electron–positron pair plasmas, the terminal speed of collimated jets is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.9c$</tex>, which is very close to the jet speed of galactic superluminal sources.

articleTitle: Substructures Revealed by the Sunyaev–Zel’dovich Effect at 150 GHz in a High-Resolution Map of RX J1347-1145
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on mapping observations toward the region of the most luminous X-ray cluster, RX J1347-1145 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ z=0.45$</tex>), through the Sunyaev–Zel’dovich effect at 21 GHz and 150 GHz with the Nobeyama 45-m telescope. While a low angular resolution image at 21 GHz (beam-size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \sigma_\mathrm{FWHM}$</tex> of 76<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {}^{\mathrm{\prime\prime}}$</tex>) shows a consistent feature with the ROSAT/HRI X-ray image, a higher angular resolution image (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \sigma_\mathrm{FWHM} =13^{\prime\prime}$</tex>) at 150 GHz reveals complex morphological structures of the cluster region, which cannot be simply described by the spherical isothermal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \beta$</tex>-model. If such inhomogeneous morphological features prove to be generic for high-redshift clusters, distance measurements to the clusters based on their Sunyaev–Zel’dovich data with low angular resolution imaging should be interpreted with caution.

articleTitle: OHS: OH-Airglow Suppressor for the Subaru Telescope
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: This paper describes an OH-airglow Suppressor (OHS) for the infrared Nasmyth focus of the Subaru telescope. OHS has the capability of eliminating 224 airglow-lines in the J- and H-bands, which are major sources of background radiation at near-infrared wavelengths up to 2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mu \rm {m}}$</tex>. Specifically, it is a pre-optics system installed between the telescope and an infrared camera/spectrograph (CISCO). The suppressor reduces sky background emissions to 1/25 and its throughput is 40%. As a result, the S/N gain achieved with OHS is more than 1 mag compared to the typical spectroscopic approach. The limiting magnitude measured during a test observing run was found to be H = 21.1 mag (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/\Delta\lambda = 210, S/N = 5$</tex>) in the standard 4000 s exposure sequence.

articleTitle: Eclipsing and Precessional Light Curves of SS 433 with Superdisks
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We theoretically calculated light curves of SS 433 during eclipse and precession, under a picture in which SS 433 consists of a geometrically thick superdisk around a compact star and a companion star filling its Roche lobe. The main parameters are the binary mass ratio, the relative thickness of the superdisk, and the surface temperature of the companion. Combinations of eclipsing and precessional light curves impose constraints on the parameter ranges. The favorite values of the parameters are a mass ratio of about 1 to 1.5 (a compact star is a black hole), a relative disk-thickness of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${25{}^{\rm {\circ }}}$</tex>, and a companion surface-temperature of 14000–20000 K.

articleTitle: First Subaru Observations of Sub-km Main-Belt Asteroids
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the first observations of sub-km main-belt asteroids (MBAs) obtained with the prime-focus mosaic CCD camera for the Subaru telescope. We detected 27 moving objects in a single image of the sky (field of view: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${27{}^{\rm {\prime }}} \times {27{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex>), whose location was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${41{}^{\rm {\circ }}}$</tex> off opposition. From their positions and projected motions on the sky, all of the detected objects were found to be new and consistent with the characteristic of MBAs. The V-magnitudes of the discovered asteroids range approximately from 19 to 24. Under some simple, but reasonable, assumptions, we estimated the cumulative size distribution for the asteroids. This is the first statistics for sub-km MBAs (the minimum diameter corresponds to about 0.6km). It is found that the slope of the cumulative size distribution for the observed asteroids is 1.0 with an error of about 0.3. We note that our slope is fairly smaller than that obtained in the past observational surveys for asteroids larger than a few kilometers (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim1.75$</tex>).

articleTitle: On the Mass Spectrum of Giant Molecular Clouds in the Large Magellanic Cloud
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Based on a new sensitive survey of the giant molecular clouds (GMCs) in the Large Magellanic Cloud, we derived the mass spectrum for them. In the mass range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim8\times10^4\,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times10^6\,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>, a power law with an index value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.9\pm0.1$</tex> shows the best fit to the data. This is consistent with numerical simulations that explain both the H i and CO clumpy distributions by Wada et al. (; ApJ, 540, 797), but is significantly steeper than that of the GMCs in the Galaxy. This may be consistent with the drastic dissipation of the GMCs in the LMC due to higher UV radiation fields than in the Galaxy.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Triple-Encounter Criterion
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The criterion for classifying triple encounters has been improved in order to cover wide triple-encounters compared to those in virial equilibrium. Its validity was confirmed by systematic numerical observations of orbits in the three-body problem with zero initial-velocities and equal masses.

articleTitle: A Diffuse X-Ray Source, AX J1843.80352: Association with the Radio Complex G28.6-0.1 and Identification of a New Supernova Remnant
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: ASCA discovered an extended source in the constellation Scutum. The X-ray morphology is an elliptical shape elongated from north to south with a mean diameter of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${10{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex>. The image center is located at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{RA}_{2000}$</tex> = <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${18{}^{\rm {h}}43{}^{\rm {m}}53{}^{\rm {s}}}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{DEC}_{2000}$</tex> = <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$- {03{}^{\rm {\circ }}52{}^{\rm {\prime }}55{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}}$</tex> (hereafter, AX J1843.8–0352). The north and south rims of AX J1843.8–0352 are associated with non-thermal radio sources C and F of the G28.6–0.1 complex (Helfand et al. 1989, AAA <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$49.125.029$</tex>). The X-ray spectrum was fitted with a model of either a thin thermal plasma in non-equilibrium ionization of a temperature 5.4keV or a power-law of photon index 2.1. The absorption column is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2.4$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.0)\times 10^{22}\rm{cm}^{-2}$</tex>, which probably places this source in the Scutum arm. With a reasonable distance assumption of about 7kpc, we estimate the mean diameter and X-ray luminosity to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 20 \,\rm{pc}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 3 \times 10^{34}\,\rm{erg} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, respectively. Although a Sedov solution for a thin thermal plasma model gives parameters of a young shell-like SNR, no strong emission lines are found with the metal abundances being <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> solar. Thus, a more likely scenario for both the radio and X-ray spectra and the morphologies is that AX J1843.8–0352 is a shell-like SNR which predominantly emits synchrotron X-rays.

articleTitle: 1998 Superoutburst of the Large-Amplitude SU UMa-Type Dwarf Nova WX Ceti
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed the 1998 November superoutburst of WX Cet, a dwarf nova originally proposed as a WZ Sge-like system. The observation established that WX Cet is an SU UMa-type dwarf nova with a mean superhump period of 0.05949(1)d, which is 2.1% longer than the reported orbital period. The lack of early superhumps at the earliest stage of the superoutburst, the rapid development of usual superhumps, and the possible rapid decay of late superhumps seem to support that WX Cet is a fairly normal large-amplitude SU UMa-type dwarf nova, rather than a WZ Sge-type dwarf nova with a number of peculiarities. However, a period increase of superhumps at a rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{P}/P = +8.5\pm 1.0 \times 10^{-5}$</tex> was observed, which is one of the largest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{P}/P$</tex> ever observed in SU UMa-type dwarf novae. A linear decline of light, with a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.10 \,\rm{mag} \,\rm{d}^{-1}$</tex>, was observed in the post-superoutburst stage. This may be an exemplification of the decay of the viscosity in the accretion disk after the termination of a superoutburst, mechanism of which is proposed to explain a variety of post-superoutburst phenomena in some SU UMa-type dwarf novae.

articleTitle: Discovery of a New ER UMa-Type Dwarf Nova IX Draconis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed a new dwarf nova, IX Dra, for 46 days between 2000 November 10 and 2001 June 17, and revealed that IX Dra is the fifth member of a peculiar group of SU UMa stars, called ER UMa stars. The light curve is almost perfectly identical to that of V1159 Ori: supercycle, 53 d; interval of normal outbursts, 3–4 d; duty cycle, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 30\%$</tex>; and the outburst amplitude, 2.5 mag. From a time-series observation during the superoutbursts, we obtained a presumable superhump period of 0.067 d. We note that some clustering may exist in the period distribution of ER UMa stars. It is needed to confirm this clustering by a larger number of examples.

articleTitle: Optical Follow-up of the GRB 010222 Afterglow by Subaru Telescope
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The optical afterglow of a gamma ray burst, GRB 010222, which was discovered by the BeppoSAX Team as the brightest one ever detected, was observed by Suprime-Cam of the Subaru Telescope at Mauna Kea. The obtained <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>-band magnitude was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$18.59 \pm 0.04$</tex> at February 22.51 UT, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$18.99 \pm 0.04$</tex> at February 22.65 UT, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$21.76\pm 0.03$</tex> at February 25.64 UT. The light curve made from all data reported so far shows the decay of the brightness with a broken power law, of which the indices are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-0.92 \pm 0.01$</tex> before and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.27 \pm 0.01$</tex> after the break. The break point of the light curve is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.73 \pm 0.02 \;\rm{d}$</tex> after the burst, which is the earliest example ever observed. A brief summary of our follow-up observations, together with the importance of the optical follow-up capable by the Subaru telescope, is described in this letter.

articleTitle: A Survey for High-Latitude Molecular Clouds toward Infrared-Excess Clouds with NANTEN
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A survey for high Galactic latitude molecular clouds was carried out toward the far-infrared-excess clouds of Reach et al. (, AAA 070.131.207) using the NANTEN telescope. All 68 infrared-excess clouds that are observable from NANTEN were mapped in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{-} 0$</tex> line of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CO. CO emission was detected from 32 infrared excess clouds, corresponding to a CO detection rate of 47%. Most of these CO clouds were identified and mapped as high-latitude clouds for the first time. The CO detection rate for the cold (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm dust} \lt 17 \,{\rm K}$</tex>) infrared excess clouds is 72%, which is more than a factor of two higher than that of warmer ones, 33%. This indicates that the cold clouds are well shielded from external UV radiation, resulting in a high CO abundance and a low temperature of the clouds. The infrared-excess clouds with no CO emission are most likely to be molecular hydrogen clouds because the temperature is similar to, or lower than, that of the surrounding H i gas. The molecular gas without CO emission seems to occupy more than 90% of the area of the infrared-excess clouds.

articleTitle: ASCA Observations of the Twin Supernova Remnants in the Large Magellanic Cloud, DEM L316
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report results from an ASCA X-ray study of DEM L316, an emission nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) consisting of two closely-spaced supernova remnants (SNRs). The SIS image shows separate X-ray sources located at the positions of the two radio- and optically-emitting SNR shells, 0547-69.7A and 0547-69.7B (hereafter, shell A and shell B). The individual X-ray spectrum of each shell is well described by optically-thin thermal emission, although the characteristics of the emission differ in important details between them. Shell A exhibits strong iron L emission, which we attribute to the presence of iron-rich ejecta, leading to the suggestion that this SNR originates from a type Ia SN, an explosion of a moderate mass progenitor. Shell B, on the other hand, has a chemical composition similar to that of the interstellar medium of the LMC, and so its X-ray emission is dominated by swept-up matter. The different spectral features strongly disfavor the hypothesis that the two shells are due to one supernova explosion into an interconnected bubble. We could not obtain evidence which positively supports the collision between two SNRs.

articleTitle: Superdisks in Supersoft X-Ray Sources
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract:
In supersoft X-ray sources the mass accretion rate is roughly equal to the Eddington rate, and traditional standard disks cannot be adequate. We thus propose a supercritical accretion disk (superdisk) for supersoft X-ray sources. We have found that superdisks exhibit various distinct features, compared with standard thin disks. The continuous spectra of superdisks generally become flat (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ 
u S_
u \sim 
u^0$</tex>), which are greatly different from those of disk-blackbody spectra, as expected in the usual accretion disk systems. This flat nature is not so prominent in supersoft X-ray sources, compared with that in the superdisk around a black hole, since the radial extension of the disk is much smaller. Moreover, irradiation becomes important for a smaller accretion rate system. The superdisk picture was applied to RX J0019.8+2156, and reproduced its spectra and optical light curves well.

articleTitle: Sunspot Magnetic Fields Observed with a Large-Format Infrared Array
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Spectro-polarimetric observations of sunspots were carried out by using a PtSi near-infrared camera (KONIC) of Kiso Observatory, The University of Tokyo, in the period of 1999 November 3–5. The camera was attached to a spectrograph of the Domeless Solar Telescope at Hida Observatory, Kyoto University. We observed the absorption lines of Fe I at 15648.5Å (Landè factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{\rm{L}} = 3$</tex>) and 15652.9Å (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{\rm{L~eff}} = 1.53$</tex>), and derived the distribution of the magnetic field strengths and inclination angles across the sunspots. The ratio of the Zeeman splitting of the two lines was derived to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.39 \pm 0.01$</tex>, while the ratio of the Landè factors is 0.51. Our data indicates that the effective Landè factor of the 15652.9Å line is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.17 \pm 0.03$</tex>.

articleTitle: Trapping of Non-Axisymmetric $g$-Mode Oscillations in Thin Relativistic Disks and kHz QPOs
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We suggest that in the inner part of geometrically thin relativistic disks there are trapped non-axisymmetric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>-mode oscillations which are excited by a corotation resonance. These oscillation modes would be the cause of quasi-periodic kHz oscillations observed in some low-mass X-ray sources.

articleTitle: High-Dispersion Spectra of NH2 in the Comet C/1999S4 (LINEAR): Excitation Mechanism of the NH2 Molecule
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out a high-dispersion spectroscopic observation of the comet C/1999S4 (LINEAR) on 2000 July 8.75 (UT). The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mathrm{NH}_2$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{A}}(0,10,0)$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{X}}(0,0,0)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{A}}(0,9,0)$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{X}}(0,0,0)$</tex> bands were extracted from the observed spectrum and compared with the modeled spectra. We developed a fluorescence equilibrium model for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mathrm{NH}_2$</tex>, in which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{A}}(0,v_2^{\prime},0)$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{X}}(0,0,0)$</tex> transitions and the radiative relaxation among the rotational levels in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{X}}(0,0,0)$</tex> were considered. The rotational structure of the spin doublet (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ F_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ F_2$</tex> levels) and the Swings effect were considered in the model. The modeled spectra are consistent with the observed spectra of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{A}}(0,10,0)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \tilde{\mathrm{A}}(0,9,0)$</tex> bands. Our results show that the fluorescence excitation and the radiative relaxation processes are dominant for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mathrm{NH}_2$</tex> in a coma of the comet at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \sim$</tex> 1 AU from the Sun.

articleTitle: Analytical Studies on the Structure and Emission of the SS 433 Jets
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have studied the structure and emission of the SS 433 jets in the X-ray emitting region and in the inner and hotter portion inside the X-ray emitting region. In order to consider the jet structure from the inner to outer regions we developed a hybrid model combining the conical beam and the model beam, whose cross section grows with the distance more slowly. We found that the jet beams in the inner and hotter portion are of two-temperature and that they emit a large amount of high-energy gamma photons. Our analyses suggest a thick absorbing envelope to exist in the SS 433 system. Based on our results, we discuss the possible acceleration mechanism for the SS 433 jets.

articleTitle: A 168-s X-Ray Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud Observed with ASCA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the detection of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$167.8 \pm 0.2\,\rm{s}$</tex> pulsations from AX J0052.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>7157 in the Small Magellanic Cloud with ASCA. The pulsations show an energy-independent sinusoidal profile. The X-ray spectrum has been described by an absorbed hard power-law (photon index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.7$</tex>) with a luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 8.8 \times 10^{35}\,\rm{erg}\,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex> at a distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60\,\rm{kpc}$</tex>. The position is determined to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{(R.A.,~Dec.)}_{\rm{J2000}} = (00{}^{\rm{h}}52{}^{\rm m}59\rlap{.}{}^{\rm s}2, -71{71{}^{\rm{\circ}}57{}^{\rm{\prime}}58{}^{\rm{\prime\prime}}})$</tex>, with an error radius of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim {30{}^{\rm{\prime\prime}}}$</tex>. We have found that a variable Be/X-ray binary RX J0052.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>7158 is located within the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30{}^{\rm{\prime\prime}}$</tex> error circle, and is also located at the edge of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10{}^{\rm{\prime}}$</tex> error circle of the 169-s pulsar XTE J0054<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>720. We therefore conclude that these are the same source, a Be/X-ray binary pulsar.

Author Keywords: pulsars: individual (AX J0052.9–7157, RX J0052.9–7158, XTE J0054–720)

articleTitle: Spiral Structures and Shocks in Accretion Discs in Close Binary Systems: the Role of the Injection Velocity at the Inner Lagrangian Point
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: In our previous paper (Lanzafame et al. 2000, PASJ 52, 515) we showed, through 2D SPH simulations, that the stellar mass ratio, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ M_{2}/M_{1}$</tex>, of a close binary system (that determines the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{1}$</tex> position and then the initial specific angular momentum at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{1}$</tex>) plays a fundamental role in the formation and development of spiral structures and shock fronts in the radial flow of accretion discs. In that work only a quasi-sonic value of the injection velocity at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{1}$</tex> was considered. In the present work we also carried out 2D SPH simulations with the aim to investigate the development of such structures, while keeping constant the mass of the compact primary (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ M_{1} = 1 M_\odot$</tex>) and the separation between the two components, and assuming as an initial condition of two different supersonic injection velocities at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{1}$</tex>, characterizing two sets of simulations. For each set we considered four values of the secondary to primary mass ratio, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ M_{2}/M_{1}$</tex>. We worked out 2D models because the damping effect of the artificial viscosity is too strong in 3D. Furthermore, the 2D environment seems to be the most suitable in order to be evidence of shock fronts in highly compressible gases. Our aim in these two works was to enhance the initial kinematic conditions (from sonic to strongly supersonic) to stress the idea that spiral structures and shock front development are influenced by the initial specific angular momentum at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{1}$</tex>. The results show that these structures are more evident with the increasing injection velocity at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{1}$</tex> and the increasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{1}$</tex> distance from the primary.

articleTitle: ASCA Identification of SMC X-2 with the 2.37-s Pulsar Discovered by RXTE
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: ASCA observed a new X-ray pulsar recently discovered with RXTE in the Small Magellanic Cloud, and detected coherent pulsations with a barycentric period of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.37230 \pm 0.00004~\rm{s}$</tex>. The position is determined within a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 30{{}^{\rm{\prime\prime}}}$</tex> radius error, which is much more accurate than that reported with RXTE. Since the position error well overlaps a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 20{{}^{\rm{\prime\prime}}}$</tex> radius error of the SAS-3 transient source SMC X-2, and since the probability that an unrelated source falls in the error region by chance is estimated to be less than 0.1%, we conclude that SMC X-2 is the 2.37-s pulsar. The X-ray spectrum in the 0.7–10.0 keV band can be fitted with a model of a power-law continuum plus a fluorescent line from neutral or low-ionization iron. The pulse profile has a single peak below a few keV and gradually changes to be a double-peaked structure as the energy increases; in particular, the iron line band (6.0–7.0 keV) marginally shows a double-peaked profile similar to that of the higher energy band observed with RXTE.

Author Keywords: pulsars: individual (SMC X-2) mdash stars: emission-line, Be

articleTitle: Discovery of a Transient X-Ray Pulsar, AX J1841.0$-$0536, in the Scutum Arm Region with ASCA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the discovery of a transient X-ray pulsar, AX J1841.0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>0536, serendipitously found in the Scutum arm region with the ASCA in two separate observations. The X-ray flux is very faint at the beginning, but exhibits two flares in the second observation. The flare flux increases by a factor 10 within only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1 \,\rm{hr}$</tex>. Coherent pulsations with a period of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.7394 \pm 0.0008 \,\rm{s}$</tex> were detected in the brightest flare phase. The X-ray spectra in the quiescent and flare phases were fitted with an absorbed power-law model with a photon index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1$</tex> plus a narrow Gaussian line at the center energy of 6.4 keV. The interstellar column density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 3\times 10^{22} \,\rm{cm}^{-2}$</tex> may indicate that AX J1841.0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>0536 is located at a tangential point of the Scutum arm at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10 \,\rm{kpc}$</tex> distance. The coherent pulsations, large flux variability, and the spectral shape suggest that AX J1841.0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>0536 is a Be/X-ray binary pulsar.

articleTitle: The Radio-to-Submillimeter Flux Density Ratio of Galaxies as a Measure of Redshift
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We re-examine the technique of determining the redshifts of galaxies from the ratio of the submillimeter-to-radio continuum flux densities based on a recently published catalog of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$850\, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> sources. We derived the expected variation of this ratio as a function of redshift incorporating the expected average luminosity and the spectral energy distribution (SED) of dust emission and the radio continuum. We find that the existing data for most of the high redshift (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \gtrsim 1$</tex>) sources correspond to our new calculation. Amongst the well-identified sources, there is none with an index significantly higher than predicted. Sources which have an index lower than predicted are either within the error zone or much lower, the latter presumably having AGN-dominated radio-continuum emission. We find the median redshift to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2$</tex>, which is consistent with that deduced by previous work (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 3$</tex>) within the error. We also discuss the various systematic effects that can affect the accuracy of the redshift estimate. We examine other methods of redshift estimation, like photometric ratio in the submillimeter and locating the peak of the SED in the rest system of the objects. We conclude that while the various methods are helpful in identifying high-redshift objects and making a crude estimate of the redshift, they are not, at present, accurate enough for a detailed study of redshift distribution of the submillimeter galaxies.

articleTitle: The Spectral Energy Distributions of Blazars and the Connections among XBLs, RBLs, and OVV Quasars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: In this paper, we introduce two composite spectral indices, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{xox}}=\alpha_{\rm{ox}}- \alpha_{\rm {x}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{oro}}=\alpha_{\rm{or}}- \alpha_{\rm{o}}$</tex>. In the composite color–color (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{xox}}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{oro}}$</tex>) diagram, there are three regions: (1) For XBLs and XBL-like RBLs, the values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{xox}}$</tex> is in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.0$</tex> -<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.0$</tex>; (2) For RBLs, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{xox}}$</tex> is in 0.0–1.5, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{oro}} \lt -0.75$</tex>; (3) For OVV quasars, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm{xox}}$</tex> is in 0.0–1.5 and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{\rm oro} >-0.75 \alpha_{\rm oro} >-0.75$</tex>. Our results support the conclusion that RBLs are intermediate between XBLs and OVV quasars, which has been given by Sambruna et al. (, AAA 65.159.120). On the other hand, based on the idea that a group of extragalactic objects which can be regarded as a category with similar physical properties must fit the same relation, using the HST new observational data, we found that there is a strong correlation between the apparent magnitude of the host galaxies and log <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> for all BL Lac objects (XBLs + RBLs), but OVV quasars lie about 4 magnitude above the Hubble line of 86 BL Lacs. This implies that all XBL-like and XBLs belong to a single category with similar physical properties, while OVV quasars and BL Lacs belong to different populations.

articleTitle: The Radio and Gamma-Ray Luminosi0074ies of Blazars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray data of blazars in the third EGRET catalog and radio data at 5 GHz, we studied the correlation between the radio and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray luminosities using two statistical methods. The first method was the partial correlation analysis method, which indicates that there exist correlations between the radio and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray luminosities in both high and low states as well as in the average case. The second method involved a comparison of expected <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray luminosity distribution with the observed data using the Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) test. In the second method, we assumed that there is a correlation between the radio and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray luminosities and that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray luminosity function is proportional to the radio luminosity function. The KS test indicates that the expected gamma-ray luminosity distributions are consistent with the observed data in a reasonable parameter range. Finally, we used different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray luminosity functions to estimate the possible ‘observed’ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray luminosity distributions by GLAST.

articleTitle: Low-Temperature Optical Properties of Silicate Particles in the Far-Infrared Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The far-infrared absorption spectra of crystalline circumstellar dust analogues (orthoenstatite, clinoenstatite, diopside, and forsterite) were measured at room temperature (295 K) and liquid-helium temperature (4.2 K). The wavelength ranges of the measurements were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\hbox{-}80\,{\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\hbox{-}80\,{\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> at 295 K and 4.2 K, respectively. The absorption bands were detected very clearly not only at room temperature, but also at liquid-helium temperature. The temperature effects were clearly observed at liquid-helium temperature, such as (1) an increase in the spectral index of the continuum, (2) an enhancement in the absorption band strength, (3) a decrease in the band width, and (4) the absorption peaks of all bands of all samples shifted toward a shorter wavelength. These results suggest that a reconsideration of the identification should be required for some absorption bands which have been recognized as unidentified bands because of a disagreement in the peak position between the observed data and the laboratory data obtained at room temperature. Our experimental data can be obtained from the web-site (http://www.kyoto-phu.ac.jp/labo/butsuri/).

articleTitle: H2 Formation in Low-Metallicity Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A possible formation mechanism of hydrogen molecules on a galactic scale is examined.
